IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS

Decisions that
shape delivery.

01Data readiness
Check access, completeness, representative examples, and the meaning of each field. A useful model or workflow depends on information that reflects the real operating environment.
02Evaluation & review
Agree what a useful result looks like, how errors are reviewed, and when a person must approve an action. Compare the solution with a practical baseline.
03Integration & monitoring
Define triggers, downstream APIs, exception queues, monitoring, and change ownership. An automation needs an operating process after its first successful run.

No. Deterministic rules are often the clearest option for well-defined processes. We select rules, statistical methods, existing models, or custom development around the problem and available data.

A defined proof of concept can test the use case, data readiness, and acceptance criteria. It should answer a specific feasibility question and inform the next investment decision.

Yes. Approval steps, review queues, permissions, and audit records can be included where the process needs human judgment or explicit authorization.

We agree evaluation criteria, relevant test scenarios, and a baseline before implementation. Results are reviewed in the context of the task, including incorrect or uncertain outputs.

We review the available APIs, authentication, data access, and event mechanisms. Integration feasibility and third-party costs are confirmed before the delivery scope is agreed.

The design should cover retries, notifications, duplicate handling, exception ownership, and a recovery path. Those behaviors are validated against the scenarios agreed for the engagement.
